_note: Views for the SCIENTIFIC NARRATIVE ATLAS design. Wireframes are given as arrays of fixed-width lines. Component ids in brackets [VU-xxx] refer to viz units in narrative_atlas_C1..C4_vizunits.json. All measured numbers are from the survey findings.

views.title: App frame (global chrome)
views.purpose: Every other view renders inside this. It carries the three things that must never be more than one keystroke or one glance away: search, the co-occurrence caveat, and the snapshot/citation identity. Described first because every later wireframe assumes it.

layout.overview: Fixed 52px top bar; optional 28px caveat strip that appears only on network/module/cluster routes; content column max-width 1440px with a 240px right rail on wide screens; 24px status footer.
wireframe: | MIRTO ATLAS   Home  Modules  Network  Browse  Tours  Verify  Evidence   [ search... ⌘K ] ◐ ⤓ |
| ⓘ Module membership is statistical co-occurrence of motif clusters across genes - not          |
|   demonstrated physical interaction.  2,620 of 166,615 co-occurring pairs (1.6%) pass.  [why?] |
| Data snapshot v1.0.0 · built 2026-09-01 · DOI 10.5281/zenodo.xxxxxxx · human (GRCh37)  [cite] |
spatial_rules: The caveat strip is NOT dismissible and NOT a tooltip. It renders on #/network, #/pair, #/module, #/cluster and inside any tour step that touches those routes. It is absent on #/gene and #/about (where it would be noise).
Omnibox is the only search entry point in the whole app; there is no second search box on the landing page. Cmd-K / Ctrl-K focuses it from anywhere.
Right rail collapses below 1180px and its contents move to the bottom of the content column.

components: [VU-C4-04] export basket button with count badge
interactions: ⌘K focuses omnibox; typing filters 17,847 symbols + 18,093 RefSeq + 20,481 ENSG + 20,481 ENST entirely client-side from the 157 KB gz index (no network round-trip)
Pasting an ENSG or ENST resolves to exactly one RefSeq (measured: every ENSG maps to exactly 1) so no disambiguation UI is shown; only the 215 genes with >1 transcript get a picker
Typing a motif string in RNA alphabet (UCUCC) is normalised to T before matching, so the manuscript's own motif names work
'why?' in the caveat strip deep-links to #/evidence/paralogy
Any table row anywhere can be added to the export basket; the basket badge counts items and the tray exports CSV/JSON client-side from data already in memory
views.entry_points: always mounted

views.title: Guided tours - catalogue and runner
views.purpose: The signature feature of this angle: a reader with five minutes reproduces a specific manuscript claim by moving real controls in the real views, not by reading a slideshow.

layout.overview: The runner is a 340px docked panel on the left (or a bottom sheet on narrow screens). The right 100%-minus-340px is the ACTUAL view for that step - the same #/cluster or #/gene or #/network the free-browsing user gets, with a focus/highlight parameter applied.
wireframe: | The Kozak          |   <<< the real #/cluster/utr5_0004 view, with the logo panel scrolled    |
| rediscovery        |       into position and one consensus row pulsing >>>                    |
| MIRTO never saw    |   | utr5_0004    ▮M6  5'UTR  1,043 instances / 372 genes            |    |
| run on this        |   |  bits┤   ▁ █▁ █▁ ▁                    C G C C G C C A C C     |    |
| yourself:          |   |  5' ▁▁▁▂▂▃▃▄▅▆▇███  3'   median_pos 0.84 - hard against the ATG |    |
spatial_rules: The panel never covers the element it is talking about; the runner scrolls the target into the visible right region and applies a 2s pulse outline, then stops.

Every step's 'check it yourself' button performs a REAL interaction (opens a table, toggles a filter, changes a sort) rather than advancing the narration. The reader can then wander off; leaving the tour keeps the current route.
The step URL is #/tour/kozak?s=3 and is shareable; deep-linking into step 3 loads the underlying route first, then the overlay.

components: [VU-C4-21] tour completion card with 'what you just verified' summary
interactions: Next/back; Esc leaves the tour but preserves the route and any filters the tour applied
Each step declares {route, focus_selector, highlight, prose, assertion, action}; the runner is ~150 lines and knows nothing about any specific view
The completion card lists every assertion the reader just saw with its measured value and a link to the source file, and offers 'add all to export basket'

tour_catalogue.title: The Kozak rediscovery
tour_catalogue.spine: M6 story card -> the prot_0040 x utr5_0004 edge (the highest-scoring pair in the whole analysis, phylo_corrected_score 1.7694, co_count 175, 23 independent clades, ZNF fraction 0.0) -> the utr5_0004 logo CGCCGCCACC -> the 372 carrier genes pre-classified by Kozak strength -> ACTB's real 5'UTR with all three of its motifs in utr5_0004
tour_catalogue.claim_verified: An unsupervised method rediscovers the Kozak consensus and pairs it with histone-fold proteins.

tour_catalogue.title: Histones find their stem-loop
tour_catalogue.spine: utr3_0463 -> eCLIP SLBP fold 48.62 (k=22/n=196) and miR-760 fold 16.99 -> the bitwise-AND carrier list with prot_0040: 17 genes, every one a histone (H3-5, H3-3A, H2AC13, H2AC15, H2AC16, H2AC6, H2AC4, H2AC17, H2AC18, H2BC13, H2BC6, H2BC21, H2BC11, H2AC7, H2AC14, H2AC12, H2BC1)
tour_catalogue.claim_verified: M6's second UTR cluster independently recovers the histone stem-loop programme.

tour_catalogue.title: The ZNF trap - why the top hits are wrong
tour_catalogue.spine: Sort the raw-NPMI leaderboard (the ONE place npmi_raw is sortable) -> prot_0228 x utr5_0020 at npmi_raw 0.897 with frac_co_ZNF 0.990 and 2 clades -> the verdict column (25/30 'ZNF clade artifact') -> the Meff gauge (18,068 genes -> 2,342 effective; 547 ZNF genes -> 9.0 effective) -> the four-condition gate that removes them
tour_catalogue.claim_verified: The filtering is doing real work, and p-value corrections alone do not remove the artifact.

tour_catalogue.title: A nuclear-degradation programme
tour_catalogue.spine: M5 story -> the utr5_0079 x prot_0072 edge (npmi_mip_APC 0.251, RNA-binding domain superfamily 11.1x, curated phase separation 9.26x) -> the 2x2 kinetics panel (PUND 1.9 / 2.7 ns / 8.0 / 15.6%; polysome t1/2 9.9 / 6.5 / 5.0 / 3.4 min; and the FOUR metrics that are not significant) -> TRA2B, the strongest nuclear decay at t1/2 24 min
tour_catalogue.claim_verified: Carrying both motifs is associated with nuclear degradation and faster polysome loading - and four of seven measured metrics show nothing.

tour_catalogue.title: Signal peptides meet GC-rich 5'UTRs
tour_catalogue.spine: M3 -> prot_0122 (LLLLLL, coverage 0.698, 415 carriers) x utr5_0090 (GCCGCCGCCGC, coverage 0.361, 100 carriers) -> the 13 co-carrier genes (TIMP3 SDC1 MEGF6 ITGA9 VEGFB GPR37 FSTL4 DKK3 CACNA2D3 RET NTN4 COL22A1 SCARF2) -> ED Fig 3k/l: max pairwise protein identity ~19%, max 5'UTR identity ~55% -> RIBOmap ER fraction
tour_catalogue.claim_verified: The module is not sequence homology in disguise.

tour_catalogue.title: Two TF programmes, one nucleus
tour_catalogue.spine: M1 vs M2 -> utr_composition.csv GC 0.344 (n=56 M1 utr3 clusters) vs 0.497 (n=66 M2) -> the 185-RBP volcano (PABPN1 20.26% M2 vs 5.21% M1, q=1.07e-134) -> the APEX table INCLUDING lamina q=0.725 and OMM q=0.551, which do not support the manuscript sentence -> MLXIPL's 7 M2 3'UTR sites
tour_catalogue.claim_verified: M2 is nuclear-retention-flavoured; two of the five stated localisation claims are not significant in the table on disk.
tour_catalogue.blocked_by: R-01 (utr3_0027 vs utr3_0227) - do not ship until the author confirms

tour_catalogue.title: Read one transcript in both languages
tour_catalogue.spine: ACTB -> the three tracks -> the 45-nt AU-rich 3'UTR element at [82,126] in utr3_0313 with TIAL1 -> the protein [23,27] DDAPR in prot_0040 -> the module fingerprint bar
tour_catalogue.claim_verified: The gene view is coordinate-correct and the annotations are real (a canonical ARE-binding protein on an ARE).

spatial_rules: The claim sentence is authored copy, but every number in it is bound to a data field and rendered from data, so it cannot go stale.
The subgraph is a small self-contained SVG (max 133 nodes for M3), NOT an iframe of the big network.
'⚠ no significant term' and '⚠ no STREME consensus' are rendered as first-class row states, because 377 of 500 utr3 clusters have no significant term - hiding them would misrepresent the module.

Module-level external validation exists only for M1/M2 (APEX, RBP volcano), M3 (RIBOmap), M5 (TimeLapse-seq) and M6 (Kozak/SLBP). M4's band renders an explicit 'no external validation dataset in this project' state rather than being omitted.

interactions: 'strict / + cross-module' toggle adds the 757 cross-module edges touching this module; for M5 this adds the 192-edge M1<->M5 link the manuscript explicitly discusses
GO panel defaults to trusted (q<0.05 AND fold>=2 AND n_fam_support>=5) per the report's own instruction; the toggle shows all significant with the counts printed (M5 593 of 1,086)
Clicking a GO dot opens the driving gene list from module_term_gene_lists.csv (2.2 MB compact form, or the per-module M<n>_term_genes.csv at 111-810 KB)
Clicking any cluster name -> #/cluster/<id>; clicking any gene -> #/gene/<sym>?from=M<n>
All five validation tables are exportable and every row shows its q even when non-significant

views.title: Meta-module map (R3, level 1)
views.purpose: The 'meta modules view' of requirement R3 at its coarsest, most legible level: six supernodes and the fifteen measured inter-module link weights, which exist nowhere on disk and are computed at bake time.

layout.overview: A single centred SVG about 760x560, with a legend strip beneath and a level switcher above. Six supernodes on a ring ordered by node_select.order_modules() so heavily linked modules sit adjacent (M5-M1-M2-M3-M4, M6 hanging off M1).
wireframe: | LEVEL:  ⦿ modules (6)   ○ clusters (519)   ○ one module   |  EDGES: ⦿ strict 2,620 ○ relaxed |
|  node area ∝ carrier genes (M3 4,348 … M6 1,562)   ring thickness ∝ intra-module edges       |
|  ring colour = mean_frac_ZNF (M3 0.003 … M1 0.062)  edge width ∝ cross-module edge count     |
spatial_rules: Only 15 edges, so all fifteen are drawn and all fifteen are labelled in the legend strip - no 'top N' truncation, because the long tail (M1-M4 = 1 edge) is itself informative.
Supernode ring encodes intra-module edge count so the reader can see M1 (774) is 18x M6 (43) without a second chart.
Hovering a meta-edge dims the other fourteen and lists its top 5 constituent cluster pairs by phylo_corrected_score.

interactions: Click supernode -> #/module/M<n>; double-click -> level 3 bipartite drill-down for that module
Click meta-edge -> level 2 filtered to the constituent edges of that module pair, e.g. M1-M5 opens the 192 edges the manuscript discusses
Level switcher morphs rather than navigates: supernodes explode into their member clusters with a 600ms transition so the reader keeps their bearings
views.entry_points: #/network (default level) ; 'Network' in top nav ; V01 funnel row 5

views.title: Cluster co-occurrence network (R3, level 2)
views.purpose: The full 519-node / 2,620-edge gated graph - the actual result of the paper - with click-a-node and click-an-edge detail as R3 requires.

layout.overview: Full-bleed SVG canvas with a 300px left control column and a 420px right detail drawer that slides in on selection. Opens on the 52-node published Fig 3e subset.
wireframe: | ⌕ find a cluster   |  [ freeze layout ] [ re-simulate ] [ ⤓ export ]  |                      |
spatial_rules: Layout is FROZEN from the bake-time d3-force run with per-module attractors and a protein-left / UTR-right bias, so deep links to 'this region of the graph' are stable and a reload does not reshuffle. 'Re-simulate' is offered but explicitly labelled as producing a non-canonical layout.

Node shape carries region (circle = protein, square = UTR) and label colour carries UTR sub-region (5'UTR #0072B2, 3'UTR #A85A00, protein black) exactly as 24_bipartite_pruned_ordered.py does - module is fill, so module and region are two independent channels.
Unassigned nodes (the 3 dyad endpoints and, in relaxed mode, more) are drawn with a dashed outline and no fill, never grey fill, because grey is M5.
Edge style is tiered: solid where a consensus PAIR exists (1,430 of 2,620 today, all intra-module), dashed where only cluster-level evidence exists - matching the published figure's own convention.
At the 519-node maximum the SVG holds ~519 nodes + 2,620 edges + 519 labels ≈ 3,700 elements, well within DOM budget and cheaper than losing hit-testing to canvas.

interactions: Click node -> V08 quick peek in the drawer; double-click -> #/cluster/<id>

Click edge -> V07 edge detail drawer at #/pair/

~ (deep-linkable)
Hover node -> its neighbourhood is highlighted and everything else drops to 15% opacity (ported from applyNodeNeighborhoodHighlight in 03.build_annotated_plotly_graph.py)

The find box accepts a cluster id, a consensus string (T/U-normalised), or a gene symbol; a gene symbol highlights every node whose cluster that gene carries - ported from findGeneHits/applyGeneHighlight in the same script
Top-N slider re-filters edges only; it does NOT re-run Louvain, and the control says so, because module assignments must stay fixed
views.entry_points: #/network?level=clusters ; meta-edge click on V04 ; 'open in the full network' from V03 ; cluster page partner table

|  ── solid = a consensus PAIR backs this edge      ─ ─ dashed = cluster-level evidence only    |

For M1 (106 nodes / 774 edges) and M3 (133/385) the column is scrollable with a synchronised edge layer; density is shown so the reader knows M1 at 0.296 is genuinely dense rather than badly drawn.

interactions: same node/edge selection as V05

views.title: Edge (co-occurrence pair) detail drawer
views.purpose: R3's 'clicking an edge shows details including annotations' - and the place where the paper's central caveat is operationalised with numbers rather than prose.

layout.overview: 420px right drawer, five stacked sections, deep-linkable as its own route.
wireframe: | co-occurrence of motif clusters across genes        |
|  npmi_raw   0.71  ⓘ not a ranking key here - see    |
|  ⓘ an RBP label means: genes carrying this motif    |
|    also tend to carry this RBP's peak in the same   |
|    UTR. fold is an upper bound for CLIP sources.    |
|  H2AC13 H2AC15 H2BC11 HMGN2 ACTB …   [ ⤓ export ]   |
| ⚠ This is co-occurrence across genes, not a         |
spatial_rules: The gate section is FIRST, above the consensus and the annotations. That ordering is the design's answer to risk R-07: the reader sees the evidence quality before they see the story.
Each gate row is a tiny bullet chart: the value as a bar, the threshold as a reference tick, a check or cross. All four thresholds are printed.
npmi_raw is shown but visually demoted (smaller, muted) with a link to the paralogy page - never as a sort key.

The consensus section degrades in three explicit tiers: (1) a consensus PAIR from consensus_pair_scores.csv.gz, available for 1,430 of 2,620 edges today (0 cross-module); (2) both endpoints' consensus lists from consensus_meta.csv (451 of 513 module clusters); (3) the most frequent literal member strings from the master table with instance counts. The tier is labelled. There is no empty state.

components: [VU-C3-36] carrier gene list with tier toggle
interactions: Carrier genes come from a bitwise AND of one Pc column and one Uc column of consensus_presence.npz, precomputed at bake time for every displayed edge - clicking any gene jumps to #/gene/<sym>?highlight=prot_0040,utr5_0004 so the gene page opens with exactly those two motifs pulsing. This is the R3 -> R1 handoff.
The resolution selector switches the carrier count between cluster level and consensus level and prints both, because the same question answers 175 or 46 depending on level
Tier A / carrier / literal follows the m4_motif_examples definition (tier A = the called instance IS the literal motif at that position); the definition is in the tooltip

views.title: Motif cluster page (R2)
views.purpose: Requirement R2 in full: for a motif, show its cluster, how it associates with protein features, and the annotations on it. Two template variants driven by region, because a single template would show empty pLDDT panels on 600 pages.

layout.overview: Header; identity band (logo + consensus + position + composition); annotation band (enrichment); partner band (the R2 answer); members band. Right rail carries stats, module breadcrumb and export.

| │  0┴──███████──  U C U C C       │ │ ⚠ 'UCUCC' also belongs to utr3_0238 - the two are    │ |
| ┌ position along the 3'UTR ───────┐ ┌ composition ─────┐ ┌ length ───────┐ ┌ score ──────┐  |
|  ⚠ No term passes the triple gate for this cluster (0 of 77 rows). Showing top terms by      |
|    nominal p, greyed, with their FDR - and instance-level frequency below.                   |
|   source   term          fold   k/n      p       fdr_cluster                                 |
|   LARP4 18 · PCBP1 15 · PCBP2 14 · DDX55 9 · UPF1 8   ▏▏▏▏▏▏  [ methods: eCLIP ▾ ]           |
|  ⓘ The manuscript nominates PTBP for this cluster from consensus-sequence reasoning, not     |
|    from an enrichment in this table. [author inference]                                      |
| WHICH PROTEIN FEATURES DOES IT CO-OCCUR WITH?    ⦿ strict (2)  ○ suggestive npmi>0.1 (18)    |
|  partner      score   npmi   co   clades  ZNF   protein features                              |
|  ⓘ 300 protein clusters co-occur with this cluster at all; 2 pass the gate.                   |
|  gene    tx         pos        sequence            score   bits  tier  annotations           |
spatial_rules: PROTEIN variant swaps the composition panel for a pLDDT distribution (medians span 0.215-0.972 across the 300 protein clusters - a genuinely discriminating ordered-vs-IDR axis) and the annotation sources become InterPro / MobiDB / ELM / IDPO / SignalP with UniProt features. UTR variant shows base composition, no pLDDT, and eCLIP / PAR-CLIP / iCLIP-P / iCLIP-CIMS / miR.
The 'no significant term' state is a designed band, not an omission - it applies to 437 of 900 clusters and to 377 of 500 utr3 clusters specifically.

The partner band leads with the PROTEIN side on UTR cluster pages, because 2,614 of 2,620 passing edges (99.8%) have a protein partner with a significant term versus only 1,180 (45.0%) with a significant UTR-side term. On protein cluster pages the same band leads with the UTR consensus.

The ambiguity warning ('UCUCC also belongs to utr3_0238') is generated automatically wherever a cluster's top consensus string appears in >1 cluster - a direct consequence of the 34,110 multi-cluster unique_motif_ids.

views.title: Gene / transcript page (R1)
views.purpose: Requirement R1 in full: 5'UTR and 3'UTR sequences with highlighted motifs, AND the protein sequence with highlighted motifs - plus the NTScore track that makes it a new object rather than a coloured-text viewer.

layout.overview: Header + availability badges; a proportional transcript minimap; three region panels stacked (5'UTR, protein, 3'UTR) each with its own track stack; a motif table; a module fingerprint in the right rail.
wireframe: | ACTB  actin beta          NM_001101 · ENSG00000075624 · ENST00000646664                      |
| 5'UTR 84 nt · CDS 1,128 nt · protein 375 aa · 3'UTR 600 nt                                   |
| ✓UniProt P60709  ✓domain track  ✓CLIP peaks  ✓genome coords   ▮M6 (1 of 6)   [⤓ FASTA/CSV]   |
| TRANSCRIPT MAP                                     colour by: ⦿ module ○ cluster ○ region    |
| ▲ you are here                          20 motifs · 3 utr5 / 4 protein / 13 utr3            |
|              DDX55 · NKRF · SUB1 · TIAL1 (eCLIP)  ← canonical ARE-binding protein            |
| ALL MOTIFS  [⌕] [module: any ▾] [annotated only ☐] [min score ──●──] [cluster ▾]  20 shown   |
| region  pos       seq            cluster    module  score  bits  annotations                 |
| utr5    5-15      CGAGACCGCGU    utr5_0004  M6      -0.41  6.1   GEMIN5 PUM1 SERBP1          |
| utr3    82-126    UAUUUGUUUU…    utr3_0313  M1      -1.31  3.2   DDX55 NKRF SUB1 TIAL1       |
| prot    23-27     DDAPR          prot_0040  M6      -0.06  4.4   Actin family (IPR004000)    |
spatial_rules: Sequence is rendered as ONE flat lane per region. Motifs never overlap within a (transcript, region) - max stacking depth is exactly 1 across all 53,367 groups - so there is no interval packing, no lane assignment and no z-ordering. This is the single biggest simplification in the whole build.
One DOM span per motif-OR-GAP SEGMENT, not per nucleotide: measured p50 89, p99 279, max 381 segments for a page showing all three regions, versus p50 1,940 / max 7,784 per-nucleotide spans.
EVERY motif span gets its own border/inset outline. 53,729 adjacent pairs abut exactly (gap 0) and 9,838 of those share a cluster - without a separator they fuse into single false motifs.
~26-31% of characters are highlighted (utr5 median 0.307, utr3 0.261, protein 0.288), so fills are subtle and saturated colour is reserved for the active colour-by channel.
UTR panels render RNA (U); the protein panel never does, because U there is selenocysteine. A [RNA (U) / DNA (T)] toggle exists for the UTRs only.

The NTScore track is real per-nucleotide data for both UTRs (from the two h5 caches, verified length-exact); the protein panel gets pLDDT + domain ruler + UniProt features instead, and a caption states plainly that no per-nucleotide score exists for protein.
Worst case to design against: NM_001351027 at 7,784 nt total and NM_001003665 at 381 segments; a 3'UTR of 7,601 nt with 182 motifs. Only 587 transcripts (3.2%) have a 3'UTR >= 5,000 nt.

interactions: Click a motif span -> popover with cluster, score, entropy, pLDDT (protein), PWM-match bits, every annotation chip, and two links: 'open cluster' and 'see this cluster in the network'
Filter chips re-render the highlight layer in place without a refetch; 'annotated only' is meaningful because 36.1% of instances have no annotation at all
Colour-by module leaves ~45% of motifs uncoloured (their clusters have no module) - the legend states this rather than letting it look like a bug
Brushing the transcript minimap scrolls all three panels; brushing the NTScore track selects a coordinate range and filters the motif table to it
?highlight=prot_0040,utr5_0004 (used by the R3 -> R1 handoff) pulses exactly those spans on load and scrolls the first into view
215 genes with >1 transcript show a picker; every ENSG/ENST resolves to exactly one RefSeq so no other disambiguation is needed
views.entry_points: #/gene/<SYMBOL> ; #/gene/<SYMBOL>?tx=<refseq>&region=<r>&pos=<n>&highlight=<clusters> ; omnibox ; every gene chip in the app ; carrier lists on V07 ; examples on V01

spatial_rules: Every facet shows its count BEFORE the click (the ENCODE-portal pattern the survey's prior-art finding recommends). Counts update as other facets are applied.
The 'none' module facet at 387 and the 'no logo' / 'no significant term' states are first-class facets, not hidden - browsing the gaps is a legitimate use of this site.
Gene tab rows carry a motif-count sparkbar (utr5 / protein / utr3 as three stacked segments) so a reader can see at a glance which genes are motif-dense.

RBP tab lists 203 names with their method-membership (166 of 203 appear in exactly one method; only 4 appear in all four) and an alias warning where the alias map applies (U2AF65/U2AF2, TDP43/TARDBP, UNR/CSDE1, IMP3/IGF2BP3, HNRNPH/HNRNPH1).

views.title: Verify a figure
views.purpose: The angle's second signature feature. For each published panel: the printed figure on the left, the live interactive equivalent on the right, and a per-claim verdict table underneath with the measured number beside the stated one.

spatial_rules: Verdict badges are exactly four: ✓ CONFIRMED, ○ PARTIAL, ⚠ CONFLICT, ◦ NOT REPRODUCIBLE HERE. Each carries the reason.

The published image is the PNG, never the .ai/.pdf. Budget-aware: Figure4.png 268 KB is inlined; Figure3.png 1.17 MB and fig1_umap_corrected_npmi.png 1.80 MB are lazy-loaded on that panel's page only.
Every panel page names its provenance folder from PANELS.md, so a reader can go from 'Fig 3e' to the code that made it.
